title: Magha Puja, the fifth time
hook: avoid evil, do good, purify the mind
tomorrow: the Buddha found his way by remembering one afternoon. which one?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Losar: a broom at the year's end, and the verse of the one good night, letting go without erasing. A fresh year. Today, the last full moon of the festival year.

Someone volunteers every Saturday, gives to every fundraiser, never misses a birthday, and is quietly furious most of the week. A good-person checklist can stop at two lines: don't do harm, do good. Magha Puja remembers a verse with three. Theravada tradition tells of a full moon at the Bamboo Grove, monks arriving from all over without being called, and the Buddha giving them a few short verses to carry. One of them is the verse a monk in a tree gave a poet a week ago, in Max Müller's translation: "Not to commit any sin, to do good, and to purify one's mind, that is the teaching of (all) the Awakened." That day was about how hard it is to live. Today is about the third line, the one that gets skipped.
screen: `A GOOD PERSON, QUIETLY FURIOUS.` → `THE BAMBOO GROVE, A FULL MOON.` → `THREE LINES, NOT TWO.`

segments.voice: So why is the mind on a list about conduct? In Pali the third line is sacittapariyodapanam: making your own mind clear. Not someone else's. Your own. The answer is in how the Buddha understood action. In the Anguttara Nikaya he says it plainly, in paraphrase: intention is what I call kamma; having intended, one acts, by body, by speech, by mind. Read that way, the first two lines are the fruit, and the third is the root. A kind deed done from a furious mind still carries the fury somewhere. That's the heart of it. So what does a clear mind look like? The Anguttara Nikaya has a short pair of lines, in paraphrase: this mind is luminous, and it is stained by defilements that arrive from outside, like visitors. Someone untaught doesn't see that, so the mind goes untrained; someone taught sees it, and trains. Notice the picture. The mind isn't rotten and in need of replacing. It's bright, with guests tracking mud through it: the fury, the craving, the grudge. In that picture, cleaning means noticing the guests, not hating the house. And it's your own house, which is why the third line says your own mind. A mind made clear isn't a new mind. It's the old one, with the mud gone. On this full moon, people walk it out: at temples in Thailand, Laos and Cambodia, they circle the temple at night with flowers, incense and a candle.
screen: `SACITTA: YOUR OWN MIND.` · `INTENTION IS KAMMA.` · `THE MIND IS LUMINOUS.` · `MUD FROM VISITING GUESTS.` · then, large: `THE HEART OF IT.`

segments.voice: Stand, if you can, and walk one slow circle around your chair or your room, the way people circle the temple on this full moon. Give each stretch a line: not harming, doing good, and on the last stretch, letting the mind settle. Then sit down where you started, and stay with that third line.
Magha Puja: the full moon of the gathering, and three lines: avoid evil, do good, purify your own mind.
Keep this one: the heart of it is the third line, a mind made clear. Seven of seven; the festival year is done.

screen: `DAY 1777 COUNTS.` → `THE FESTIVAL YEAR · 7 OF 7.` → `TOMORROW: HE FOUND HIS WAY BY REMEMBERING. REMEMBERING WHAT?`

howItsDone: On the Magha full moon, Buddhists in Thailand, Laos and Cambodia go to the temple, hear a sermon, keep the precepts, and at night walk around the temple holding flowers, incense and a lit candle.

fork.setup: your friend helps everyone at the food bank but snaps at her sister all week. by the Magha Puja verse, what's missing?
options: the third line: clearing her own mind, where the deeds start.
nothing; doing good is the whole of the teaching.
more good deeds, enough to outweigh the snapping.
fork.reveal: the verse has three lines, and the Buddha calls intention itself kamma. the deeds grow out of the mind.

chat.says: ông says my mind is 'bright, just muddy.' ava says that's a nice way of saying messy. is it?
options: it's from a sutta: the mind is luminous, stained by defilements that come and go.
ava's right. the mind is dirty all the way through, so you start over.
it means stop thinking. a clear mind is an empty one.
chat.meaning: The Anguttara Nikaya calls the mind luminous, stained by defilements that arrive from outside; the third line of the verse is cleaning your own.

tie.story: At the full moon gathering, the Buddha gave three lines; the third is make your own mind clear, and a sutta calls that mind luminous.
tie.friend: Mai can tell Ava that Ông meant the mud is a guest, not the house.
tie.you: which of the three lines needs you most this week?

Magha Puja.meaning: the full moon remembering the gathering of monks and their verses

Bamboo Grove.meaning: a park given to the Buddha, where he often stayed

sacittapariyodapanam.meaning: Pali: making your own mind clear

kamma.meaning: action, which the Buddha roots in intention

Anguttara Nikaya.meaning: a collection of the Buddha's discourses, grouped by number

luminous mind.meaning: the Anguttara's picture of the mind as bright, stained by visiting defilements

sources.quoted: Not to commit any sin, to do good, and to purify one's mind, that is the teaching of (all) the Awakened.

sources.ref: Anguttara Nikaya 6.63 (Nibbedhika Sutta: intention is kamma)
Anguttara Nikaya 1.51–52 (the luminous mind, stained by incoming defilements; the taught and untaught)

notes: The Magha Puja gathering (monks arriving at the Bamboo Grove without being called, on the Magha full moon) is the commentarial tradition, voiced as 'Theravada tradition tells'; no count of monks given. Confirm.
Dhammapada 183 quoted from Max Müller (1881), as on days 694, 1424 and 1770; please check the wording against the 1881 text.
Sacittapariyodapanam (sa-citta, one's own mind; pariyodapana, cleansing) glossed as 'making your own mind clear'. Confirm.
AN 6.63 paraphrased: 'Intention, I tell you, is kamma; having intended, one does kamma by body, speech and mind.' Confirm.
Candle procession around the temple (wian thian) given without a count of circuits. Confirm.
Shape: wisdom (one question: why is the mind on a list about conduct?). Mai's arc: Ông calls Mai's mind 'bright, just muddy'; Ava questions it.
Surprising fact: the Buddha says intention itself is kamma, so the third line is the root of the other two.
